'''Ursula''' "'''Uschi'''" '''Steigenberger''' (25 April 1951 — 12 December 2018) {{post-nominals|country=GBR|OBE}} [[FInstP]] was a German condensed matter physicist and director of the [[ISIS neutron source]]. She was one of the founders of the [[Institute of Physics]] Juno Award.

== Education ==
Steigenberger was born in [[Augsburg]]. She studied physics at the [[University of Würzburg]], where she remained for her graduate studies. She earned a PhD in [[condensed matter physics]] under the supervision of [[Michael von Ortenburg]]. For her doctoral thesis she designed a stress rig, which allowed her to apply uniaxial pressure to single crystals of [[tellurium]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.osapublishing.org/captcha/?guid=AC10FBC9-B563-BA17-31C8-AEF6B8811A28&AspxAutoDetectCookieSupport=1|title=Captcha|website=www.osapublishing.org|access-date=2019-03-13}}</ref> After earning her PhD in 1981, Steigenberger worked in various magnet labs, including the [[Cnrs|CNRS]] Grenoble High Field Magnet Facility in Grenoble and [[Lebedev Physical Institute]] in Moscow.{{citation needed|date=March 2019}}

== Career and research==
Steigenberger joined the [[Institut Laue–Langevin]] in 1982.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.isis.stfc.ac.uk/Pages/Uschi-Steigenberger-receives-OBE.aspx|title=ISIS Uschi Steigenberger receives OBE|website=isis.stfc.ac.uk|access-date=2018-12-14}}</ref> She worked on the '''''PR'''ogetto dell'<nowiki/>'''I'''stituto di '''S'''trutura della '''MA'''teria del CNR'' (PRISMA) spectrometer with collaborators in Italy, and continued to work with them on the motion of molecules.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lnl.infn.it/~prisma/it/index.html|title=INFN - Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare|website=lnl.infn.it|access-date=2018-12-14}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gov.uk/government/news/top-female-scientist-honoured-for-a-lifetime-in-physics|title=Top female scientist honoured for a lifetime in physics|website=gov.uk|language=en|access-date=2018-12-14}}</ref> She worked on [[cadmium telluride]] that had been alloyed with [[magnesium]].<ref name="SteigenbergerLebech1986">{{cite journal|last1=Steigenberger|first1=Ursula|last2=Lebech|first2=Bente|last3=Galazka|first3=Robert R.|title=Neutron scattering studies of a dilute magnetic semiconductor: Cd1-xMnxTe|journal=Journal of Magnetism and Magnetic Materials|volume=54-57|year=1986|pages=1285–1286|issn=0304-8853|doi=10.1016/0304-8853(86)90820-6|bibcode=1986JMMM...54.1285S}}</ref> Here she met British physicist [[Keith McEwen]], whom she married in 1986 before the couple moved to the [[United Kingdom]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.isis.stfc.ac.uk/Pages/2009-A-year-around-ISIS.aspx|title=ISIS A year around ISIS|website=www.isis.stfc.ac.uk|access-date=2019-03-13}}</ref>

Steigenberger joined the [[ISIS neutron source]] in 1986.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.helmholtz-berlin.de/pubbin/news_seite?nid=14632;sprache=en;seitenid=74699|title=Uschi Steigenberger receives prestigious British medal for her service to the sciences|website=helmholtz-berlin.de|access-date=2018-12-14}}</ref> She was initially responsible for the PRISMA spectrometer, leading a collaboration between the [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council]] (EPSRC) and Italian [[National Research Council (Italy)|Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche]].<ref name="SteigenbergerHagen1991">{{cite journal|last1=Steigenberger|first1=U.|last2=Hagen|first2=M.|last3=Caciuffo|first3=R.|last4=Petrillo|first4=C.|last5=Cilloco|first5=F.|last6=Sacchetti|first6=F.|title=The development of the PRISMA spectrometer at ISIS|journal=Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research Section B: Beam Interactions with Materials and Atoms|volume=53|issue=1|year=1991|pages=87–96|issn=0168-583X|doi=10.1016/0168-583X(91)95449-N|bibcode=1991NIMPB..53...87S}}</ref> PRISMA was used for inelastic neutron scattering from single crystals.<ref name="SteigenbergerHagen1991" /> It can measure the change in scattering during the application of temperature, pressure or magnetic fields.<ref name="SteigenbergerHagen1991" /> Steigenberger was made one of the ISIS Excitations Group leaders, becoming the first woman Division Head in 1994. She attended the Oxford School on Neutron Scattering in 1991.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.oxfordneutronschool.org/history.htm|title=History of the Oxford School on Neutron Scattering|website=oxfordneutronschool.org|access-date=2018-12-14}}</ref> In 1996 Steigenberger coordinated a workshop on pulsed neutron experiments.<ref name="SteigenbergerMcEwen1997">{{cite journal|last1=Steigenberger|first1=Uschi|last2=McEwen|first2=Keith|title=Pulsed magnetic fields and pulsed neutron sources|journal=Neutron News|volume=8|issue=1|year=1997|pages=2–3|issn=1044-8632|doi=10.1080/10448639708231951|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/314912}}</ref> She served as director at the ISIS neutron source from 2011 to 2012.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://physicsworld.com/a/uk-physics-hit-by-new-cuts/|title=UK physics hit by new cuts|date=2009-06-25|website=Physics World|language=en-GB|access-date=2018-12-14}}</ref> She worked with scientists from Norway to create Larmor, a high-intensity small-angle scattering instrument that uses a beam of polarised neutrons to study the movement of atoms in a material.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://phys.org/news/2012-06-uk-netherlands-collaboration-state-of-the-art-neutron-super-microscope.html|title=UK-Netherlands collaboration will build state-of-the-art neutron super-microscope|website=phys.org|language=en-us|access-date=2018-12-14}}</ref> Steigenberger served as Chair of the [[Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin]].<ref name=":1" /> She retired from the ISIS neutron source in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.isis.stfc.ac.uk/Pages/OBE-for-Uschi-Steigenberger.aspx|title=ISIS OBE for Uschi Steigenberger|website=isis.stfc.ac.uk|access-date=2018-12-14}}</ref> Her work was recognised by scientists all over the world, developing important partnerships with Japan and Italy.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.isis.stfc.ac.uk/Pages/Dr-Uschi-Steigenberger.aspx|title=ISIS ISIS mourns the death of Dr Uschi Steigenberger OBE, former Director and friend|website=www.isis.stfc.ac.uk|access-date=2019-03-13}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Steigenberger was shortlisted for a [[WISE Campaign]] Lifetime Achievement Award.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wisecampaign.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/wise_awards_2013_role_models_booklet_final_041113.pdf|title=WISE Lifetime Achievement Award|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2018-12-14}}</ref> She was a Fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]], and part of their review of women in the physics workplace that led to the Juno award scheme as well as being a member of their Science Board.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=http://www.iop.org/news/16/jan/page_66765.html|title=IOP members are recognised in New Year Honours|website=iop.org|access-date=2018-12-14}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://www.iopblog.org/remembering-uschi-steigenberger/|title=Remembering Uschi Steigenberger|last=McNair|first=Rosslyn|website=The Institute of Physics blog|language=en-GB|access-date=2019-03-13}}</ref> In the [[2016 New Year Honours]] she was appointed [[Officer of the Order of the British Empire]] (OBE) for services to science, which she collected in 2017.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=https://www.vaizey.com/news/ed-vaizey-steps-secure-award-obe|title=Ed Vaizey steps in to secure the award of an OBE|website=vaizey.com|first=Ed|last=Valzey|year=2017|language=en|access-date=2018-12-14}}</ref> This OBE was honorary as Steigenberger kept her German citizenship whilst working in the UK.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4" />

==Death==
Steigenberger was diagnosed with [[pancreatic cancer]] in January 2017, and died on 12 December 2018.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://stfc.ukri.org/news/stfc-mourns-the-death-of-leading-physicist-dr-uschi-steigenberger-obe/|title=STFC mourns the death of leading physicist Dr Uschi Steigenberger OBE - Science and Technology Facilities Council|author=Anon|year=2018|website=stfc.ukri.org|publisher=[[United Kingdom Research and Innovation]]|location=Swindon}}</ref>
